Einfach erschreckend!!!
Apr 2026 • Friends
Secret Garden, Ho Chi Minh City
The only good thing about this place is the rooftop location. The terrace on the 5th floor looks nice and has potential — but that’s where the positives end.
Getting there is already a bad start: the elevator wasn’t working, and you have to go through a rather shady, uncomfortable entrance. Not exactly a welcoming experience.
The food was disappointing. What we received looked quite different from what was shown in the menu — misleading at best.
The service, however, was the worst part. The waiter was rude, dismissive, and clearly uninterested. When we asked simple questions, the attitude was sharp and unfriendly. No professionalism at all. When we left, there wasn’t even a basic goodbye.
Overall, a very unpleasant experience and definitely not what you expect from a place with such a nice setting. A real disappointment — especially as it happened at the end of an otherwise great holiday...

Dear Guest,

Thank you for providing us with your honest feedback regarding your recent visit to Secret Garden (158 Pasteur). We were deeply saddened to read about your experience, especially as it occurred at the end of your holiday. Please accept our sincerest apologies for failing to meet your expectations in almost every regard.

We understand that the entrance through an old apartment building and the climb to the 5th floor can be unexpected. While the elevator is managed by the building complex, we truly regret that its malfunction made your arrival difficult.

More importantly, we are very concerned about your comments regarding our service and food. Providing rude or dismissive service is completely against our standards, and we will be addressing this with our floor team immediately to ensure such an attitude is never repeated. Thank you again for your feedback, as it helps us improve.

Horrible!
Mar 2026 • Couples
Horrible is the only word that fits: at the bottom of a dark courtyard where dozens of motorcycles are parked, you have to climb 4 awful floors on foot because the elevator is condemned by chains and padlocks. It's already sad, dirty, unseemly. Arriving on the top floor, we see a kitchen (photographed by another customer and visible on this site), not very tasty. Let's go into the large open-air room. Well, we're reassured that sounds more inviting. We wait... A lot... After twenty minutes, I get up and go check with a waiter to finally take our order (other people entered after us had already been able to place an order.)
The dishes are coming... Mine was really not good: the pork I had to roll in a stiff rice leaf with some vegetables and herbs was overcooked and totally tasteless. I left much of the dish. 
Belly a little hollow, I thought I was going to have dessert for once. Bad took me: again a good 15 minutes waiting without any server moving to see if by chance a client would need anything. So I finally get up. I approach the kitchen: one of the waiters was on his cell phone and two waitresses were playing with a small dog... I demand the menu again. We study the short dessert menu... then wait. Nobody's coming. We ended up getting paid and leaving. Don’t waste your time, breath and money: go your way.

The springrolls were really bland. The pork ones were basically a split pork sausage tied to a mini ricepaper rice packet with nori, and the beef ones were loaded with bland beef mince and gristle. Really terrible stuff. Nothing remotely like described or shown in the menu.

Just when you think you've hit a culinary low point in life, you get a bowl of cold rubbery squid that looks like it was dusted with a mixture of flavorless sawdust and flour. No salt, and definitely no chili. A little bowl of store bought sauce was probably the highlight - but the bar could not have been set much lower.

The prawns skewers looked like they were reheated with a blowtorch after being cooked earlier that day.

All of this (2 plates of springrolls, 1 really bad plate of rubbery squid dust, and flavorless prawns) as well as two overpriced local beers for a ridiculous price of about 900,000vnd.

Shameful.

My worst dining experience in Vietnam.

Actually, the worst dining experience of my 42 years spent on this planet so far.

A hidden gem for Vietnamese food lovers
Nov 2023 • Business
It is located on the rooftop of an old building on Pasteur Street, in the heart of Ho Chi Minh City. You can access it by taking a small elevator or climbing up the stairs. Once you get there, you will be greeted by a cozy and charming atmosphere, with wooden tables, colorful lanterns, and plants everywhere. The staff is friendly and attentive, and the menu offers a variety of dishes from different regions of Vietnam. You can find salads, spring rolls, noodles, rice, seafood, meat, and vegetarian options. The portions are generous and the price is reasonable. One of the best dishes to try is the chicken and herbal hotpot, which is a traditional dish from the north of Vietnam. It is a soup with chicken, mushrooms, herbs, and spices, served with rice noodles. It is very flavorful and warming, perfect for a cold day. The hotpot comes with a clay pot and a burner, so you can cook it at your own pace and enjoy it while it is hot. The restaurant also has a selection of drinks, such as fresh juices, smoothies, beers, and wines. You can also order desserts, such as ice cream, cakes, or fruits. Secret Garden Restaurant is a great place to have a delicious and satisfying meal, while enjoying the view of the city from the rooftop. It is a hidden gem that you should not miss.

Excellent for gluten free!
Feb 2023
We ate at this restaurant on two separate occasions. The menu is gluten free, unless otherwise noted, so it was a godsend for me! 

It is amazing that while it is in the center of a busy location, the actual restaurant is a calm respite from all of the noise and traffic. The first time, we came for a late lunch, and it wasn't very busy at all. The second time though, was just before a big dinner rush, and we didn't have a reservation. Since it was still early though (5:30), they could accommodate us on the condition that we leave by 7 pm - no problem! 

I had the same dishes both times - beef steamed in a banana leaf with vegetables, and grilled eggplant. They were so mouth-watering, I had to have these dishes both times! My dish was also served with a phenomenal green chili sauce - we were able to get a list of the ingredients from the chef - hopefully Google translate gives me an accurate translation! 

The setting is beautifully decorated, with colorful lanterns and strings of lights.

A hidden gem…
Oct 2022 • Couples
Finding this place is challenging, but once you locate the right alleyway and staircase, keep the faith and take the stairs as far as you can.

A uninspiring entrance leads to a wall of colourful lanterns, then the real experience begins and the sound and smells take over. A rooftop garden with a lovely rustic feel in the centre of Saigon, away from the chaos on the streets below. The clientele is a healthy mix of locals and visitors and there is a real buzz in the air as the staff flitter between tables and the kitchen at a pace.

The menu is varied with a modern take on traditional Vietnamese classics. Once you finally attract staff to your table, food arrives quickly afterwards and was delicious. It did not disappoint.

The restaurant would suit both couples or larger groups, but my advice would be to book ahead as it is clearly very popular even on a Monday night! A great spot for those moody selfies so make sure you have plenty of charge left on your phone, as this venue will certainly provide that opportunity!!

Dinner alongside a live cockerel
Mar 2019 • Couples
Our guide-book's description of the Secret Garden was spot on – down an alley filled with motorbikes and on the top floor of an elevator-free building. This meant four floors, up past apartments and what might have been offices in a rather faded ambience. We were told that we would have a forty-minute wait. Reserve a table for the next night just in case, said the others on arriving, and so I did.

The following night we puffed up the stairs, passing a couple with a child’s stroller descending. Our reservation had held, but we had to wait five minutes for a table. There was the same bustle here as there had been in Morning Glory and Nha Hang Ngon, but it was smaller than either and with slightly fewer pretensions to smartness. The menu was shorter; the food when ordered came randomly. The anchovies I ordered were off, so I had fried corn with prawn and onion, a starter which was the last thing to be brought, and mackerel with tomato sauce and rice, no more than ordinary. My wife had some spare ribs and a bit of catfish. As a final nod to the culinary newcomer of the holiday we had to have a dish of morning glory. 

It was a jolly enough meal, enlivened by realising that on the very small ornamental garden by our table was a cockerel in a cage. It got some of the rice that my wife decided not to eat, while an opportunist cat turned up and panhandled bits of her catfish.

Incredible find!
Apr 2019 • Couples
We are on our honeymoon & needed to find somewhere for dinner after a day of sight seeing in Ho Chi Minh City. My husband did some research online and came across this place. I double checked it with Trip Advisor and, happy with our find, we set off. We stumbled across it (very nearly walked past it as if you don't know what you're looking for, you could very easily miss it). It is nestled down a little alley in between houses. However, there is a lit up sign outside to help locate it. We wandered in and walking up the stairs with the little posters on each floor, we weren't sure what to expect at the top. What we did not expect was the prettiest rooftop restaurant we had ever seen. It was pretty busy for a Tuesday night at 8.30pm. We did not book, but I think we were incredibly lucky to get a table without a reservation. The staff were friendly & like a previous reviewer said, their service can be a bit casual in that they don't keep bothering you, or ask if the food is good - they know it is. However, if we needed anything more, we asked and it appeared quickly. Service was good when it needed to be. 
We weren't sure what to order but the menu is in good English and has photos of every dish which we found really helpful. We decided to go for two appetisers, a stir fry, a main meal and jasmine rice (all you can eat for 10,000 dong each!). That was plenty for two people. The food was absolutely delicious. Some of the best food we have eaten in Vietnam during our stay. 
The restaurant itself was gorgeous - fairy lights, balloon lanterns & lots of green plants with quirky tiling. We even heard a cockerel crow at one point, but we didn't see it. 
This place is absolutely stunning and really good value for money (we were surprised by how small our bill was for all that food plus two drinks each). One to definitely return to next time we are here.

The service was a little subdued and we didn't feel the same friendliness we'd experienced at other restaurants in the city. Perhaps this was because as it was their lunchtime (they ate near us and seemed in high spirits) a shift change or break was about to occur.

We ordered a variety of small dishes and they were a mixed bag - see photo descriptions for details. A couple of them were really nice, some were OK and others were forgettable.

I am glad we did not believe what those negative reviewers said about Secret Garden. It is an amazing restaurant with a clever mixture of creative and authentic Vietnamese food! The service was exceptional and accommodating for family. The price was more than fair and reasonable for the quality of food you get. The ambience was hips! The deco itself (including those on your 4 flights of stairs up) was artistic. Bring an empty stomach and order as many dishes as possible. Drink the lemongrass lemonade - refreshing. My son had 3 glasses of this. Eat the grilled pork wrapped in lemongrass stalk. The grilled pork rib was also so very tender. The field crab soup brought tears to my wife as it was like what her late grandmother used to cook for her (she’s Vietnamese). The grilled “bacon” is in fact grilled pork belly, which is probably the most popular dish. We also loved the stir-fried baby octopus! Clean, efficient and smart service. The restaurant is run by a group of young, enthusiastic and friendly team. Saigon should be proud of herself - the new generation is making its wave!

Cozy place in an interesting location

This is my fifth visit to Vietnam. We decided to visit this place after recommendations from Lonely Planet Vietnam book. Interesting location of the restaurant - you have to walk in to a apartment complex where people live and at the top floor is the restaurant. We went at night at 9pm. Pretty place, nice decorations, great view. I see from other reviews that the service can be variable, but the service was good at the time when we were there (maybe because I speak Vietnamese?). The place was 80% full when we were there, and in Vietnam the service funny enough tends to be better when the restaurant is full. When there are few guests, the waiters (often youths) will just hang around, talk to each other, sit on their phones and make comments about their guests in their language. 

We ordered clay pot basa fish, stir fried "Ly" flowers, fried lotus with minced pork and 2 glasses of lemongrass lemonade. Great authentic food! Total price 350 000 VND for two people. The appetizers are at the same price point as the main dishes. We also suspect the prices has been increased since it has become quite famous amongst tourists. Seemingly no locals at the time we were there. Lonely planet book lists 50 000 - 110 000 VND per meal per person.

All in all - highly recommended, especially at night.

Secret garden
Jun 2018 • Couples
Hi all
We recently visited the Secret garden roof top for another dining experience in wonderful Saigon. Now for us on this trip it was the first time eating in a relative “restaurant” styled environment. We had so far only eaten “street food” and it’s been pretty darn good thus far and we will continue to eat this way. Anyway back to our culinary experience at Secret garden. 
Once you locate the access point and enjoy the old world stair climb you will find yourself passing the kitchen and entering into a cloud of garlic, chilli, lemon grass and all things good to open out into a devine tropical roof top city oasis. Strings of low fused lighting hang loosiely across your heads. Clusters of greenery promote from oversized planters separating diners. Subtle tones of local music combined with global tongue create this magical roof top oasis 
Once seated, staff were friendly and responsive to our choices from the menu. Drinks served, starters out very quick. Mains out in good time to be ready to eat again. 
With four of us dining and generally all very much foodies, we really gave that menu a workout. So, octopus, prawns, baby clams, beef, pork and those chicken wings. Only real disappointment was the beef. Also a great little wine list to tempt you. Personally I think Vietnamese food goes well with cold local beer. 
So our meal was done. All of us sitting like fat Buddha’s feeling good. Don’t forget the stairs, they were still waiting for us. My wife and I are still sub 50 oursfriends sub 60 (just). The stairs are steep and four floors may find some folks doing it a little tough. Take your time. 
So to wrap up. Secret garden was a treat for us. It was a great place to meet with friends and enjoy food. As far as value for money it was on the higher side of price for us but I guess somebody has to carry the produce up those stairs..
I personally totally love sitting on undersized plastic chairs in dark ally ways eating whatever it is being served. 

Secret garden 7.5/10

The restaurant is up four flights of stairs on a roof terrace which was pretty with views of the city. The food was good on the whole, and quite reasonably priced. Unfortunately the waiting staff really let the place down. They were unfriendly, did not smile or welcome you to the restaurant. The dishes came out as they were ready, fine as we’d ordered a few to share, except they forgot the rice we had ordered so we had to ask again and this came after all the other dishes. The restaurant was about half full, with lots of staff around. However, they all spent most of the evening sitting around and playing on their phones, so it took a bit of time to get any attention. The final straw was the bill - they charged us for three rice (there were only two of us, and it was supposed to be unlimited rice per person), and an additional portion of ribs. They sorted this out quite quickly, then on looking more closely the second time we realised they had also charged us for a different - and more expensive - beef dish. It took some time to get the bill back this time, then we waited ages again to actually pay. Change was dumped on the table without a thank you or an apology for the mistakes. Totally put us off, a shame as it has spoilt an otherwise decent meal.

I have eaten twice at Secret Garden over the past 3-4 months. During my first visit, I had the overwhelming feeling that all they wanted me to do was eat my food quickly and leave, so that they could process more customers.

Go check this place out now!!
Jan 2018 • Friends
We dined here on our last day of a 2 week trip throughout Vietnam. It was the absolute best of our eating experiences. The menu offers a good variety, descirbed in English. We ended up with 5 dishes. They were all distinctly Vietnamese. Each dish was subtly different from each other. It was certainly authentic, but with an elevated taste. Yes, you can probably get cheaper food on the street corner. But, Secret Garden is a real resturant. I live in San Francisco and consider myself a long time foodie.(but not bougie) The decor of Secret Garden is straight out of any foodie magazine, down to the plates and cups. The rooftop dining room is spacious, thoughfully designed, even the bathroom has style.
The food was amazing. So tasty and simple, but bold and individually unique. The difference between a street vendor and Secret Garden is technique. I loved all the food I had in Vietnam.There is something to admire and crave about the delicious, greasy ban xeo, the 45 cent delicious but ordinary banh mi, the 25 cent grilled pork stick from the nice lady on the street. I can't say it enough- Secret Garden's food is discerning, elegant plated. When the owner talks about the "concept" of the place- that means with direct intent to create a comprehensive experience for customers.
I can see that Secret Garden is more expensive than the pho corner stand. But by western standards, it was still dirt cheap. And c'mon, we all had enough extra money to travel to Vietnam. Don't start with the false indignation of being price gouged!
Yes, you paid for your napkin, a pretty crappy one at that. But you do realize that 2000 VND is 8 cents 0.07 Euros 0.062 British Pound 5.26 Indian rupee, you get the point...Maybe, Secret Garden, you might prominently state the napkin charge on your menu. That way, if someone is trying to budget, they can forego the extravagance, they can choose to use their sleeve instead.
Finally, yes, the service could be a tad better. But it wasn't like I was thinking the staff was talking crap about me or spitting in my food. They all just seemed to be kids, without much experience. Perfunctory, ernest., maybe insecure. Maybe, Secret Garden, you might give your staff some tips on how to be more open hearted, have fun....but I'm not really complaining.
Secret Garden, I loved my experience there, thank you!!

I love this restaurant, but today you screwed up
Nov 2017 • Friends
So today I booked a table for 3 people at 6:30 pm. My friends had just arrived to visit me all the way from Amsterdam and I had told them about the secret garden and how great the food, ambience, and view was. All of which is still true, anyway we arrived and had some delicious starters and mains in one of my favourite spots.

We sat talking for a few minutes and said it's been a long day shall we order a little more food, some wine, and of course some deserts. This was their first time in Vietnam and we were ordering different things so they could sample some of the best food on Vietnam for their first meal. This was only 45 minutes in and it is a Monday night, so there was no rush to order those extra things right? Well your head waitress clearly disagreed... She came over and before I could say 'menu', she said you have to give up your table for more customers and pay. I was shocked as people had arrived before us and were not made to leave. Her tone was rude, and I really wondered how on earth such a rude woman was in charge of customer service especially at one of Saigons most famous restaurants. I understand the restaurant was full but that's not my problem, your staff should handle bookings better and actually think. Really you should have compensated us by reducing the bill or offering a freebie, or a substantial discount for next time.

We went elsewhere for wine, desert and a little more food which is a shame for you as that easily totaled 1.5 million dong more, they also got a tip which your staff missed out on due to the incompetence and rudeness of the madam running the restaurant.

I have given an average rating because I hope this is a one off and that you will fix the problems that she caused. I hope that their will be a next time, as I have just been promoted to manager and was hoping to invite 10 people, 3 of which are co managers. We were planning to come on pay day next month to celebrate. I was also planning a romantic date with someone, who would really love to come to the secret garden. I could always take them all to com moc in d2, and give you a terrible rating, or alternatively you can fix this, apologize, and make an offer and I can give you the very good rating to match my experience the other 6 times I have come in the last 9 months. I can also bring these people and all the money that comes with that. You choose!

food ok - service bad when busy - setting nice
Nov 2017 • Friends
I went to this place numerous times before as it is one of the few places I can recommend as VN food for visitors from overseas. This is due to the setting and the reasonable food. 

The last two visits were very different and I had bad experiences with service and food. This can happen once, but after the second time it is a no-go. 

1. Setting
The setting is nice, on top of a house in the middle of District 1. 

2. Reservation
Reservation is stronly recommended, refer to my service comment

3. Food
The food is diverse VN style. Normally quite good, but the last weeks and months it has lost its appeal. It is not fresh anymore and rather disappointingly average. The spring rolls are just fried to death, therefore tasteless and the fried xoi is not crispy as is is supoosed to be. The beef was overcooked and spices non existent. 
This can happen, the chef can have a bad day. It however happened too often the last weeks and months. So I believe this has become common. 

4. Service
The service used to be nice and attentative. This has changed since the place has become busy. 
We always book a table as this place becomes busy after 7pm. it is beyond my understanding why we had to wait for 20 minutes last itme despite having booked a table. Once we had our dinner, one service lady came and asked if we could pay now - obviously because there were people waiting to be seated. we declined as we wanted to have desert. The lady brought the bill anyway. This was beyond my understanding. 

4. Conclusion
The service went down compared to how it was when the restaurant opened. The food as well. I cannot recommend this place anymore.

If you go, be prepared to climb to the 4th floor roof deck of an old apartment building. You will find a wonderful atmosphere for a group or romantic dinner. Though service is slow, it is an interesting place to eat.

FOOD
While some of the food offerings had wonderful combinations...pork wrapped shrimp covered in sesame seeds, or lotus root stuffed with pork...the preparation left something to be desired. The dishes were dry and overcooked.

The vegetable dishes were better prepared, and the hot & sour fish soup was very good.

GENERAL

Authentic experience
Aug 2017 • Friends
We were recommended to this place by our AirBnB host. This rooftop restaurant is on the rooftop of a 5-storey block down an alley near Nha Hang Ngon. There's no lift and if you are doubting whether it's worth the climb halfway up, yes it is. 

We were there, without a reservation, at around 7:45 pm on a weekday night, and the restaurant was already packed. We were told that we would have to wait for 20-30 minutes, but we decided to have a go. Luckily we got a table within 5 minutes. Reservation is therefore highly recommended. As with most restaurants in HCM, and as expected for a rooftop restaurant, it is not air-conditioned, and their (very tamed) cat would wander around from table to table. 

Their menu offers a wide array of authentic Vietnamese food that you wouldn't find else where in other restaurants. Most dishes go well with steamed rice, and rice are served free-flow and charged per head. Come with friends and family so you get to share more dishes. 

Drinks were a bit on the sweet side but generally very good.

A glimpse of the past with current amenities
Apr 2017 • Couples
The secret garden is not a culinary marvel, yet I would easily return and recommend it to anyone. Don't get me wrong the food is good, maybe even really good, but what it does have that is truly magical, is provide an accesible portal into authentic Saigonnese urban life.

The secret garden isn't as much of a secret anymore, and it isn't even much of a garden. Sure a few rooftop plants and a couple cooped roosters; What it really is is an authentic glance into a way of life few people outside of Vietnamese culture ever get to see.

Partially hidden in a Saigon alley and atop of an old residential/commercial building, this restaurant invites its patrons into the "real" Saigon. Into the past that hasn't been modernized yet, where entire families live in a single room. Where live wires hanging from the walls and shut down elevators are old news. This place makes a "pour and stir" Irish pub seem like a joke. There is no fake here. This is the real deal.

And if you think this is an authentic Vietnamese eatery, it isn't. There are plenty of those, from plastic chairs on the side walk to fine Vietnamese dining in colonial buildings. Instead, the eating experience is clean, affordable and tasty. Nothing magical in the food, the magic comes from the setting.

One slight disappointment came from the tea service. I am hoping the hot tea isn't always served in a water glass.

Other than that, the service and staff was great, cleanliness surprising despite the setting. Everything you would want and more.

Great atmosphere

Be ready to wait on a Saturday night as this place is jam pack by 7pm till 9pm. Not knowing much about it, the name "secret" drew me to hike up 4 flights of stairs. I was totally surprise by this cute restaurant.

It was lively filled with tourist on this fateful Saturday night. I was alone and getting hungry. I made it known to the staff that I am alone and don't mind sharing a table. I was finally seated after 10mins with 3 other group of tourist from Brazil, Australia and Japan. 

The good was good but not fantastic (small portion) and price which i though was fair. I ordered garlic fried rice, sweet & sour pork, sesame chicken. All was good and as it did felt like mamma's cooking. Very casual food and don't expect much more then that. 

What I love about this place is the Atmosphere!!!! Wow... it was buzzing and full of energy. The place is well decorated and love breeze being on top of the roof. 

I think this place get a few bad review from guest is that they are just a popular place and cant take care of everyone when it's so busy. Remember eating at a busy cafeteria?

Feb 2017 • Couples
This hard to find but very popular restaurant is really worth seeking out. After you find the right alleyway follow the signs to the right building and then just keep climbing the stairs until you get to the top. Even with a booking they won't save a table for you, but the turnover is so quick you won't have to wait long. 
The food is fantastic and very good value. It comes out very quickly, but not necessarily in a sensible order. Expect your mains to arrive before your entrees and your rice not to arrive until the end of the meal. It's almost impossible to get the waiters attention to order any more food or a second drink, so get your order right the first time and maybe order two drinks at the start.
Despite this it's worth if for the great vietnamese food done well. Drinks are cheap and theres a full selection of vegetarian and vegan items clearly marked.
Best food we ate in vietnam, but they need to stop treating customers like the enemy!

The Secret Garden Restaurant is on Pasteur not far from the inland end of Nguyen Hue Boulevard but can be tricky to find. Down a non-descript alley and then up six flights of steps to the top floor of the building, however, the effort is definitely worth it. If you are in HCMC, do not miss this restaurant! We ate here twice during our stay in HCMC, dinner and lunch, and the food, service and ambiance was wonderful both times. It has an open air feel, and is decorated in style that reminded me of Hoi An. The open air section can be covered by awnings if the weather turns bad. I will eat at the Secret Garden Restaurant again next time I am in HCMC.

Vietnamese Food On Rooftop of Old Building
Jun 2016 • Couples
Aptly named, this restaurant serves home cooked style Vietnamese food on the roof top of an old building right in the heart of Saigon city. In all honesty, the food is nice but nothing truly memorable. What conquers the heart here is the entire experience of dining here, right from the moment you walk into an old alley in search of the old staircase leading up 5 floors by foot to the roof top restaurant. Along the walk up the stairs, you pass by very old style mailboxes (please see pics) which would give you a pretty good idea how old the building is. Sometimes you get to peek into the hallway of lower floor neighbours and you get a glimpse of the past so to speak. The restaurant itself is very tastefully done, with a olden day charm and style which simply has to be experienced in person to fully appreciate its beauty. Here, dining under the open skies infuses a sense of relaxation and tranquility (unless there are some noisy tables celebrating some occasion or gathering). Even so, the feeling that time has slowed down persists perhaps owing to the many plants and flowers all around the tables or is it the 2 adorable resident cats roaming around lazily rubbing themselves against the legs of diners (please see pics). Personally I enjoyed playing with the cats which to me is part of the entire pleasant dining experience. While I may not remember what food I ate here, I do remember the overall dining experience to be a very enjoyable one. And that I would return again if given the chance and this is a place which I would most definitely recommend highly to friends visiting Saigon.

Hidden Roof Top Gem
Jul 2016 • Friends
Lets just start by saying, this is not the rooftop you go to for the views, it is for the ambience and eating outdoors. Getting to the restaurant requires you to navigate what looks like a scooter parking lot o get to the entrance that leads to the stairs. This place is very difficult to find and you will probably have to ask someone when you get nearby. You then walk up about 5 flights of stairs and enter a roof top restaurant/garden. It's a great setting.

We ordered a few dishes and the food came out very quickly and was amazing. Some of the best food I have had in Vietnam. The fried prawns in sesame is a must and was sensational, this must be the first item you order.

Now the bad part- The restaurant had many Westerners in there and I'm sure it's because of trip adviser as it's too hard to find otherwise. I received my bill and paid, when they returned my change without the receipt I was expecting 117,000 VND change and then I would of tipped them. I received 17,000. when I asked to see the bill again the waitress simply walked up with the missing 100,000 and never even looked at the change already provided to me. Which to me tells me they deliberately short changed me and was seeing if I would notice. So please beware.

So how do I rate this? Was amazing food, great atmosphere but then deliberately trying to rip me off. They probably would of got the 117,000 VND if given a choice but the move really left a sour taste in my mouth.

Pretty, expensive restaurant with poor hygiene - don't touch the ice
May 2016 • Couples
We came here on recommendation from our accommodation being told it would be a delicious and romantic restaurant for our last night on holiday. The place admittedly is beautiful in a great rooftop location and the food while bland and expensive (an extra 10% VAT as well as being charged for napkins was a nice surprise on the bill) wasn't really bad, just mediocre for the price point we were paying. The terrible thing about this place is the lack of hygiene. 

My partner and I had been travelling around Vietnam for two weeks and eating at much more budget eateries than this one, at all of them we were assured that the ice was not made with tap water as this should be avoided at all costs due to sanitation issues. Stupidly, we did not ask at this restaurant and assumed due to the price and location they would have abided by these basic hygiene standards. We were wrong and almost missed our flight the next day with terrible vomiting from this restaurants thoughtlessness. 

If this restaurant hadn't been so cheap as to skimp on hygiene basics I would have given them 4 stars because the place really is beautiful and the food isn't terrible. As it is, I am very disappointed and I recommend others to go to any one of the hundreds of other restaurants in the city that would offer them a better experience for much less.

Jan 2016 • Couples
We found this place from visiting the Hard Rock Cafe (I always collect a shirt and pin); we were going to eat there but then decided to ask the staff for good Vietnamese food and was directed here. Although I love Asian foods, I honestly haven't really eaten much Vietnamese food. It's true it's not easy to find (we used Google Maps) but asking around helps. It was quite humorous as we climbed some dodgy stairs from a dodgy alleyway, but the Secret Garden certainly lives up to its name in decor.

It's a rooftop restaurant on the 4th level of a shabby looking building with beautiful decor and lots of string lights and lanterns. The ambiance definitely screams "secret garden". There is a little flower garden in the middle of the seating area, and some cute little kittens ready to play with patrons. I know a lot of patrons would find this annoying but luckily we are cat lovers.

The food is in small portions, but very cheaply priced. I think for the starters and even mains ranged about 2-4 USD a plate. We ordered pork ribs, pork and snail stuffed snail shells, beef and leaves (stirfry) and deep fried cat fish. And WOW!! All of them were delicious! It was my first time trying snail and it was goooood. They brought several different types of sauces and they were all tasty.

The only downside (and was quite a major one) was when my husband was looking out to the edge of the rooftop and said, "What's that? Some kind of exotic creature?" NO, it was a giant rat.... ugh. Living in the rafters of the building. That was a bit off-putting but luckily we had finished our meal. Please get rid of the rats!

The secret's out!
Jan 2016 • Couples
Even mid-week, if you want to have dinner before 8:30-9:00 pm, make a reservation. This place is popular and small. 
All reviews are subjective, so I'll tell you what I love: dining al fresco, wooden tables and chairs, cozy ambience, and of course delicious food! This place was exactly what I love about traveling in warm climates. We went there for dinner our last two nights of the five we were in HCMC. Too bad we didn't find this place sooner. We don't normally do repeats, but when you strike gold you just stop prospecting. It's rustic, charming, and the 4-story climb up the old apartment stairwell to the rooftop garden after ducking into the alley to find the place gives it quite the adventure feel. We had 7 dishes the first night with 2 beers, and 6 the next night again only repeating one dish--their specialty, the snails! Each dinner cost $30, give or take a couple bucks. A steal compared to the air-conditioned tourist trap restaurants most guides and concierges might direct you to and we loved every dish we tried! Not as cheap as street food, but just as authentic in my book--with charm to boot. Again, it depends on what you're looking for. I am also quite sensitive to msg and I could not detect a smidgen of it. All the flavoring came from fresh meats, herbs, spices, and chilies! I am NOT ALLERGIC to msg, so if you ARE, I am not making any claims that the food is entirely msg-free.

This is not a restaurant we would have found on our own and even with trip advisor reviews as a guide, it would take a mildly adventurous tourist to head down the wide laneway and the up 5 flights of stairs to find the restaurant (some fun signs encourage you to continue the trek upwards). We had no idea what to expect but when we got to the top it opened up into a roof top oasis. Rustic timber, brightly coloured lanterns, lotus leaves bursting out of huge clay pots and staff dressed in very simple linen uniforms. Our guide told us that the restaurant and uniforms were designed to replicate a simple village restaurant. The food came out relatively quickly and was super tasty. The salads are so fresh, the sour soup with red snapper was really tasty, as was the beef with morning glory - and my whole family went nuts over the spring rolls (we had to order a second serve). The fresh juices were the refreshing hit that we needed after walking for a few hours. We were a party of 7, there was something for everyone, we left comfortably full and it cost us just over 1M dong ($60 Aust). Nice clean bathroom to boot!
We will be going back before we leave.

Mediocre, At Best

When we arrived in HCMC, we were told that this was a real gem of a restaurant, and a favourite among aficionados of authentic VN cuisine.
We decided to give it a try, and braved the 4 flight walkup after entering an alley and a dim corridor. If you have mobility issues, it is four full flights so plan accordingly.
The rooftop setting is very nice...simple, but attractive, with a buddha set in a garden.
The menu is extensive and easy to read. Prices are mid range (by western standards).
For a refreshing drink, try the lime/lemongrass over ice...very nice with the right amount of zest.
We ordered spring rolls, plain rice and a catfish dish. The spring rolls were "OK", but the catfish was mushy and very fishy-tasting. We eventually ordered some ribs and left the catfish essentially uneaten.
The wait staff was largely indifferent, even though there was only a smattering of guests at the time. Often, we had to wave to the waiter/waitress to catch their attention, and I actually had to seek out the server to prepare our bill (she was busy texting on her phone).
No one queried why we didn't eat the fish, just collected our plates and presented us with the tab. 
Now for the finale...it's a small thing, but sometimes it is exactly the small things that gall.
When we first arrived, there were no paper napkins on the table, and they brought us two moist serviettes in a plastic wrapper. Lo and behold, they charged us for the serviettes! 
It's not a lot of money, but it didn't add to the experience...would have been nice to have an option, or at least a signal there was to be a charge.

Startling Ambiance Hidden inside the City
Jun 2015 • Friends
I hadn't looked this place up on TA and I was taken here by a couple of friends, one Vietnamese, and her expat boyfriend. I really had no idea what I was getting into, and hopefully you'll stop reading here and just got and be surprised.

If you really want to know more, fine. The place is "inconveniently" located up a few flights of stairs, so expect to be slightly out of breath when you arrive. You'll arrive and be seated (it was raining when we went, so the place was empty, but we couldn't sit in half of the areas because they were soaked) and then you'll probably be awestruck at the design. From the living roof to the brilliantly colorful lamps, there's a lot to look at. Even the menu was too pretty to stay concentrated and make a decision.

Regarding the food, I would recommend going here with a group because there are a lot of dishes and you should experience, just like everything in Vietnamese cuisine, a lot of flavors at once. We got a shaved coconut salad, tomato-sauce-drenched-mackerel, a fried rice dish, sweet and sour pork, and fried anchovies. The anchovies, which felt like eating fries, were probably the weakest of the dishes, but everything else was fantastic.

The drinks were stunning too. We each got fresh fruit juices. Would recommend 10/10 the lime and lemongrass juice. I've never had anything like it before but could drink it every day.

I think the highlight of the place for me, above all else, is the service. You're essentially waited-on very quickly and the food comes out HOT within 2 minutes of your order (which just boggles my mind). It helps to have a Vietnamese friend go with you because sometimes they are out of items and you can get recommendations.

Oh, and finally--try the dessert. If you've never had it, it's delicious. The creme corn was especially amazing. Everything about all of the dessert--like the rest of the food on the menu--is completely authentic, so you'll truly be getting a taste of Vietnam.

Hidden Gem. Our Best Meal in Vietnam
Mar 2015 • Friends
You know how sometimes you enjoy a place so much that you hesitate to tell others because you don't want it to get overcrowded and change? This is one of those places.

I'm not really sure how this place isn't rated higher, though perhaps our experience was somehow exceptional.

Most importantly: the food is fantastic. In a country of fantastic food experiences, our meal here stood far and above the rest. 

The location is conveniently close to the city centre. The surroundings are beautiful - the name is well-deserved. Atmosphere and decor were perfect for my tastes: busy with energy, but not too loud for conversation; simple, elegant design.

There were no negatives, from my perspective. The restaurant was very busy, and I felt the staff did an excellent job of balancing quick service with friendliness.

My only recommendation would be to clarify the availability process. We were initially told on arrival that there was no availability. I requested a reservation for later, which wasn't really understood (this doesn't appear to be common in Vietnam). After a bit of persistence, we were told that we could stay, but that we would have to wait about 10 minutes for a table. The staffed seemed to be worried that this would be an issue for us - I would have gladly waited much longer than this!

I can't wait to return on my visit to Vietnam.

Pretty and unusual setting - fabulous food
Feb 2015 • Couples
The wonderful secret of the Secret Garden is now not so secret after all as it was deservedly busy each of the 3 times we visited. Best to book for sure.

Its a 4 floor climb to the restaurant once you find the little apartment block its situated in.

Once there it's decorated very stylishly using reclaimed timber and the roof garden is a verdant oasis complete with a couple of chickens and a friendly cat; nooks and crannies are filled with happy diners.

The food is wonderful and the portions good; no starter main thing going on as everything served is a similar size so think large tapas and go for 3-4 dishes between 2
along with the yummy steamed rice. Then order more if there is still a gap.

We first went just a day after 'Tet' New Year so with markets being closed our favourite choices were not available. This caused no problem at all as to try the rest of the menu we simply came back for lunch one day and dinner the next. 

The service is prompt and friendly, there's good music and a lovely mix of both locals and Johnny Foreigner. The price of both food and drink are very reasonable considering its located in Ho Chi Minh City

Baked fish, ribs anyhow, spring rolls, just deliciously fill your boots then rebook and go again and try more stuff..

The Secret Garden has a facebook page also which is how we reserved each time we visited as they monitor it very well.

We will certainly be back - yum yum!

The restaurant is in a small street in a central area of Saigon. As most people know, it's located at the back of a motorbikes parking lot. That's part of its charm, just like the fact that it is on the 4th floor with no elevator. When you go upstairs, little signs help motivating you and finding your way. Wonderful experience not to be missed
Jul 2014 • Couples
Located in a nondescript run down 'alley way', after navigating the 83 stairs up to the restaurant you are greeted by........... a secret garden on the rooftop of the block of apartments. The setting is beautifully done with city skyline views and the restaurant set up is very intimate, relaxed and laid back (until the resident roosters start up!).
Everything has been very well put together from the cool wine list printed on the label of a wine bottle, the waiters peasant uniforms, the display of crockery for sale, the mud brick walls and the menu.
The menu is beautifully photographed and the food is as good as in the photos.
My wife and I had a selection of appetizers: the corn, shrimp and onion, shrimp balls in banana leaves, 5 spice ribs and the stuffed squid and finished off with a mixed fried rice. All dishes were excellent, cheap (65-95k each) and portion sizes were very generous. 
Probably the best meal we have had in VN and we've been here for nearly 6 months.
Biggest disappointment is that after 6 weeks in HCMC we have only just discovered Secret Garden and we're leaving HCMC in two weeks. Still enough time for a few more visits before we leave though!

I visited Secret Garden after a recommendation from a local foodie and was definitely glad I went. Although it's tucked away in a tiny building it's actually very very easy to find and in a very central location. You do have to walk up 4 flights of stairs but that was actually what made the wonderful restaurant such a surprisingly find. At the top of the stairs stood the amazing restaurant which was just lovely. It was a very hot day yet the restaurant, which was not air conditioned was cool and breezy. There's a charming rustic feel about the whole place, with sturdy wooden tables and cutlery stored in cylinders like you to in old noodle joints. The service was great - I was dining alone and started ordering whatever sounded good on the menu. The waiter bothered to go through the trouble of searching for pictures on his phone for my reference and even warned me that I might not like a dish I wanted to order because it was a little exotic. What they did recommend me to order was amazing. I love eating rustic simple food and this definitely fit the bill. I had the pork in lemongrass, a simple boiled vegetable dish and pork with coconut - all dilicious. I also liked that these are not Vietnamese dishes commonly found in Vietnamese restaurants abroad - you can only get this kind of food in Vietnam. All in all one of the coolest restaurant experiences - despite me dining alone and not having much time to enjoy the food.

Torn between wanting to tell everyone, and wanting to keep it a secret for myself!
Sep 2013 • Solo
I was in Saigon for one extra night after my flight was delayed and decided to visit the then newly opened Secret Garden on a whim. It really is hidden away down a little alleyway, and then hidden again up 5 flights of stairs, but it is so worth the effort to find it as you find yourself in a wonderful little gem of a place - lovely chilled out atmosphere, higgledy pigglegy decor, plants and books everywhere...and absolutely delicious food! It's sometimes a bit depressing arriving somewhere and asking for a table for 1, but the staff were very welcoming and looked after me without being annoying or overly attentive.

I had no idea what to order as everything looked good so I asked the waiter to help. He first asked how hungry I was (very) and then recommended 4 dishes and also the pomegranate juice (SO good I had 2). I had a watercress salad, lemongrass and pork, an amazing coconut dish and squid - it seemed like a lot of food, infact it was a huge amount of food, but the flavours were so fresh and delicious that I had little trouble polishing it all off! They were holding a photo exhibition in the restaurant and I was encouraged to walk around and see the photos which was a good way to help with the full feeling!

Secret Garden is a place you could easily spend many hours with friends and you would probably forget the time, it is relaxing and a very pleasant place to spend an evening. Food is certainly not typical Vietnamese food but there are very local elements about it. I will run back there on my next trip to Saigon!

A hidden treasure
Oct 2013 • Business
This new restaurant is a great example of a new generation of individual entrepreneurial spirit in Vietnam.

The owner has taken some great Vietnamese style cooking ability and paired it with a "unique" and beautifully simple location to create a restaurant that should be on your to visit list.

Finding it:
The Secret Garden is an excellent name for this restaurant, as it is just a little difficult to find. It's also too new to be in the rough guide or lonely planet books which may explain the healthy mix of cool urbanite Vietnamese and western travellers... Most probably trip advisor readers! 

As others have noted the restaurant lies down an ally off Pasteur street. More helpfully it's on the north side of Pasteur street, and a few meters east of a much more obvious restaurant *name*

There is a sign to the left of the ally entrance, but like many in Vietnam, it can easily get lost amongst the myriad of signs that's surround it, so keep your eyes peeled.

The ally is full of motorbikes, as are many in HCMC, but walk to the end and an open stairway to the left is your stairway to this hidden treasure. If you wait long enough at the entrance way, a local with no grasp of English will take you to the stairwell. Normally I shun such unasked for help, expecting to be led to a shop selling something I don't want, but in this case the locals are actually directing you the last 20m to where you want to go.

The restaurant is at the top of a 5 storey residential block, and whilst the lift may or may not be "coming soon" you will need to walk the stairway in the meantime. This is a mini adventure in it'll as you walk past peoples homes, and catch a glimpse of apartment living for thousands of Vietnamese residents who don't enjoy the luxury if western style hotels the city offers.

The garden:
The restaurant is very tastefully done, a rooftop garden elegantly and simply decorated with wood and plants makes for a contrast to the ascent you make before hand. The air is cooler than at street level and the fans and some outdoor AC units keep the temperature in check. The view is interesting, with some sky scraper slitting up the night sky around you, but be aware your not the tallest building in the vicinity.

The food:
The menu is reasonably priced with a meal for 2 including local beer for around £12-15. It is local style, so don't expect a burger!

The service:
The service is very good, with the staff speaking enough English to make recommendations and check things are ok.

Recommended? We've already told our friends who are heading to HCMC about this restaurant.
